name: A Second Life
summary: An exhibition identity that asks what makes ordinary objects worth keeping, with an editorial balance of object and interpretation.

palette.name: Text
palette.evidence: Dominant text-run color in source richSlides

palette.name: Primary
palette.evidence: Observed direct source color; this reusable accent role is an editorial choice, not an inferred original token.

typography.usage: Titles and short section openings; source slide 8 / request.
Reading text, supporting labels and detailed explanations; source slide 8 / status.

recognitionRules: Use Baskerville titles with Gill Sans curatorial text.
Keep warm paper, charcoal and rust as a quiet material palette.
Give each concept object a clear image, caption and interpretive question.
Keep collection access and opening status separate from the creative premise.

principles: Invite attention before offering interpretation; keep object facts and imaginative response distinct.
Use the identity’s sample as a rhythm and vocabulary reference, not as a factual project claim.
voice.sample: What makes an ordinary thing worth keeping?
voice.sampleStatus: Original fictional brand copy authored for this guide, not a quotation or factual claim.
avoid: Avoid prescribing a viewer’s feelings or implying unverified provenance.
Avoid invented testimonials, performance claims and quotation attribution.
voice.secondaryExample: Look at the edge, then read the record.
voice.cadence: Short opening, concrete follow-through; vary sentence length for explanation.

logoDirection: Use A SECOND LIFE in Baskerville with a small interrupted baseline. No recycling arrows; the identity concerns interpretation as well as reuse.
invariants: Use Baskerville titles with Gill Sans curatorial text.
Keep warm paper, charcoal and rust as a quiet material palette.
Give each concept object a clear image, caption and interpretive question.
adaptations: A wall label retains the question and object record.
A proposal expands access and production requirements behind the same editorial front.
Keep the full name with any new symbol until the audience can recognize it independently.

fonts.sourceFontDependency: Baskerville is a separately licensed/system font; not bundled.
Gill Sans is an Apple/system or separately licensed font; not bundled.

clearSpaceRule: Keep one half of the main wordmark cap height clear around the full silhouette, including its source-derived supporting device.

minimumSize.status: production minimum based on rendered 220/180px wordmark and 32/64px symbol inspection; verify again for unusual substrates
